correctness.rationale: For n≥5 the five-column predicate is exactly equivalent to locating-total domination because distinct unselected vertices with equal nonempty signatures must have a common neighbor and hence cyclic column separation at most two. Consistent four-column overlap states encode all circular words. The standalone Python code reconstructs the entire exact 256-state transition graph, computes all entries of min-plus powers eight and eighteen, and verifies the shift by eight in each of 41,728 finite positions with identical infinity patterns. Therefore the ten-step recurrence follows algebraically for every n≥8. The same integer computation establishes the base minimum sizes at n=5,...,17, and an independent whole-graph exhaustive checker verifies the predicate and smallest sizes at n=3,...,8. The proof does not infer an infinite statement from finite samples; it uses a fully checked finite matrix identity as a lemma. Scientific limits and dependency on reproducible computation are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2021 primary publication states an upper bound and proposes an incorrect five-residue equality formula. A previously indexed 2026 finding already establishes the 8+5t counterfamily, so it is expressly excluded as novel. The present stronger conclusion fixes all ten residues, proves sharpness or one-unit obstruction at every order, and identifies n≡6 mod10 as the sole exceptional residue. Targeted indexed searches did not identify coverage of the all-order formula or the exact finite-state ten-step matrix identity. The closest inaccessible full text is declared as residual risk, not silently cleared.
